title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck builds an axiomatic formalism of 'figures'. The data are a poset (M, ≤) of elementary pieces (for example simplices, or principal figures) and a set 𝓕 of figures. Each figure F is identified with the down-closed subset F̃ ⊂ M of elementary pieces it contains. On p.17 (1.34), F is of finite type iff F̃ is a finite union of principal down-sets M_{≤x_i}.

This page says that, given (M, ≤), the essential extra datum is a binary relation on M, written with a crossed/bowtie symbol ≬, that is symmetric and reflexive (1.35). It must also be stable under passing to smaller elements (1.36): X ≬ Y, X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y ⇒ X' ≬ Y'.

Grothendieck claims a bijection between such relations and families 𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(M) satisfying the previously listed conditions, plus the requirement that the F ∈ 𝓕 be (unions of) figures of finite type. The natural dictionary is:
- X ≬ Y iff M_{≤X} ∪ M_{≤Y} ∈ 𝓕, i.e. X and Y are 'compatible' or jointly fit into a figure.
- Conversely, a finite union of M_{≤x_i} is a figure iff the x_i are pairwise ≬-related.
- General figures are the down-closed sets that are (filtered) unions of these.

Reflexivity says each principal down-set is a figure. Down-stability says sub-figures of figures are figures. Thus 'morally' (M, 𝓕) ≡ (M, ≤, ≬ satisfying (1.36)). This is a poset-enriched version of 'clique complexes ↔ graphs', or of coherence spaces: the figures are the down-closed ≬-cliques.

He remarks that in practice, in almost all examples, one defines the figures from M together with ≤ and a 'relation de disjonction' ≬. He then turns to the second relation ≪ (strong inclusion / 'being in the shadow of'). This relation is used mainly to form ombres ('shadows'), starting with the 'grandes ombres', defined on the next page as Omb(F) = {X : X ≪ F}. The purpose is a combinatorial, poset-theoretic substitute for topology (open sets / shadows) in his 'tame' analysis situs, to be valid both for set-theoretic figures in a set L and for finite affine simplicial figures over an ordered field.
errors: The claimed bijection needs a 'pairwise determination' axiom: a finite union of principal down-sets is a figure as soon as all pairwise unions are (a flag/clique condition). Without it, 𝓕 is not recovered from ≬. Presumably this is among the 'conditions énumérées précédemment', but it is not stated on this page.

Naming tension: he calls ≬ a 'relation de disjonction', but a reflexive relation stable under shrinking (1.36) cannot be literal disjointness. It must be read as compatibility / 'allowed to coexist in a figure' (e.g. simplices meeting along a common face, or disjoint). Disjointness would be irreflexive, though it is also down-stable.

ideas.what: Encoding the set of figures over a poset M by a symmetric reflexive, downward-stable relation ≬ on M. Finite-type figures are the down-closures of finite ≬-cliques.
ideas.modern_name: clique (flag) complex of a graph; coherence space / stable-domain style 'cliques'; poset version of an independence/compatibility relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Flag complexes: classical combinatorial topology. Coherence spaces: J.-Y. Girard (1986-87), building on G. Berry's stable domains (late 1970s).
ideas.where_published: Not in the published corpus as far as I know; the 'figures/ombres' formalism of the 1986 Analysis situs notes is unpublished.

ideas.what: Plan to define 'ombres' (shadows) via a strong-inclusion relation ≪ between elementary pieces and figures, as a combinatorial replacement for open sets.
ideas.modern_name: well-inside / way-below relation (proximity spaces, frames/locales, continuous posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Efremovič (proximity spaces), Scott et al. (way-below relation in continuous lattices, 1970s), frame/locale theory
ideas.where_published: The tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5), but the ombre/≪ formalism itself is not there.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's reduction of a figure structure to (M, ≤, reflexive symmetric down-stable ≬) is essentially a coherence-space / clique-complex structure on a poset, appearing in a tame-topology context in 1986. This is contemporaneous with Girard's coherence spaces in denotational semantics. The link between his figure formalism and stable domains / coherence spaces has not been drawn in the literature.
missed.quote: "moralement", le couple (M, 𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(M)) équivalait : la donnée de ≤_M et de ≬ satisfaisant (1.36).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly a historical curiosity. It suggests his combinatorial analysis situs could be phrased in domain-theoretic terms (cliques, way-below relation for ombres). That could be relevant to o-minimal/tame topology or digital topology formalizations. The mathematics on this page itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine (if neat) observation that figures over a poset are determined by a pairwise compatibility relation. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'figures/ombres' programme and for its unremarked resemblance to coherence spaces.
transcription_corrections: 'satisfaisant les conditions [?] immédiates précédemment' should likely read 'satisfaisant les conditions énumé-rées précédemment'.
'il y a corr. bijective entre l'une de telles relations sur M, et d'une de 𝓕' is better read as 'entre l'ensemble de telles relations sur M, et l'ensemble des 𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(M)…'.

Last lines: 'Elle sert pour les [?] constructions surtout à former des ouverts, je commence par les grands ouverts' should read approximately 'Elle sert pour l'instant surtout à former des ombres, je commence par les grandes ombres'. This is consistent with Omb(F) defined on p.19.
'qu'on définit les ouverts...' is uncertain in the image; the word is short, possibly 'les ombres' or 'les objets', not clearly 'ouverts'.
'que les F ∈ 𝓕 soient [-denses-] à type fini' is perhaps 'soient [deleted word] de type fini' / 'réunions de figures de type fini'.
